reasoning: mixbench is a real benchmark (mixed compute/memory-bandwidth roofline sweep), so it is scheduled rather than skipped. Every profiled variant reports capability.accelerator=none and empty gpu_libs, so per the GPU rule I do not request a GPU and instead take the portable OpenMP CPU build. Among the CPU builds, :latest is the generic (non micro-arch pinned) mixbench-cpu image — the tags like :cpu, :cpu-zen4, :c2d, :c4, :azure-hpc bake in -march=alderlake/zen4/cooperlake/etc. and could SIGILL on a mismatched node, and :hpc7g is arm64-only. The binary is pure OpenMP with mpi=none, so it runs as 4 independent per-node instances; no fabric is required and network is left unconstrained (portable), letting it match either efa or ethernet clusters. Command is just the benchmark binary, which sweeps its own kernel/operational-intensity range and sizes its working set from the node; no input deck exists. Memory: mixbench allocates a single large device/host buffer (a few hundred MB up to a couple GB by default) plus OpenMP thread state, so it will not OOM on a modest node, but 0-16GB is tight if the buffer scales with a many-core node, hence 16-64GB per node as a safe estimate at 4 nodes. Duration 600s covers the full intensity sweep on all 4 nodes.
